summary: Meta's CEO published a long-form essay laying out Meta's philosophy on "personal superintelligence," arguing for individual empowerment over centralization, describing product directions (personal AI agents, free/paid tiers with a compute auction), and proposing policy positions on export controls, government-lab collaboration (sharing intermediate training checkpoints), open-source AI, and a new internal board-level governance process for approving model safety criteria.

practices.reason: Meta describes a new internal governance step where its board approves safety criteria and reviews release compliance, a process pattern engineers could note but not directly replicate or run themselves.
practices.quote: Meta is implementing a governance structure that gives our independent board of directors the power to approve the safety criteria for releasing models and reviewing whether each model release adheres to the criteria.

notable_reason: A rare, extensive public philosophy and policy statement from a frontier lab CEO addressing centralization, export controls, government collaboration on model checkpoints, and internal safety governance, likely to shape industry and regulatory debate.
